en: The Chapter on Non-Proliferation, Concerning the Question on Inference.
7. The Question on Yakkhas “Venerable Nāgasena, are there in the world those called yakkhas?
“Yes, great king, there are in the world those called yakkhas.”
“But do those *yakkhas*, venerable sir, pass away from that womb?
“Yes, great king, those *yakkhas* pass away from that womb.
“But why, venerable Nāgasena, is the body of those dead *yakkhas* not seen, and why does the stench of a corpse not waft forth?”
“Great King, the bodies of dead yakkhas are visible; the stench of their corpses also wafts abroad.

Great King, the bodies of dead yakkhas may appear with the color of insects, or they may appear with the color of spiders, or they may appear with the color of ants, or they may appear with the color of moths, or they may appear with the color of snakes, or they may appear with the color of scorpions.”
“Sometimes he appears in the form of a bird, sometimes he appears in the form of a centipede, sometimes he appears in the form of a deer, and sometimes he appears in the form of a wild animal.
“Who else, venerable Nāgasena, apart from one as wise as you, could answer this question when it was asked?
Thus ends the seventh chapter, the Chapter on the Yakkha.
